basis.method: Qualitative classification of already documented relief candidates; no new terrain features or numeric elevation values are inferred.

elevation_classes.R1: High-relief candidate: mountain belts and highlands explicitly present in prior relief notes.
elevation_classes.R2: Intermediate-relief candidate: lower plateau, hills, or uplands; relative rank remains provisional.
elevation_classes.R3: Low-relief candidate: basin or broad lowland candidate; not necessarily a closed depression.
elevation_classes.RX: Unclassified: side, continuity, or relief relationship remains unresolved.
elevation_classes.rank_meaning: Qualitative within-continent design classes only; not absolute heights and not a validated elevation ordering.

continent_assessment.drainage: Unknown; basin may be open, closed, or a broad lowland.

drainage_topology.rule: Do not assign basin closure or river direction until continuous relative elevations, saddle elevations, and outlet thresholds are specified.

limitations: All classes remain NON-CANON and qualitative.
R1-R3 labels do not represent fixed height intervals or meter values.
Ranks must not be compared across different continents.
Some continents have insufficiently specified relief for a complete hierarchy; these areas remain RX.
The three basin candidates retain unresolved outlet status.
No river centerlines, lakes, deltas, wetlands, glaciers, or named waters are added.
No plate boundary type, motion, volcanic arc, or fault is inferred.
The inherited SVG coordinate scaffold is not a validated map projection.
